solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Impertinent male adolescent with yen to change sides

indicators.note: the Y (yen) at the front of the word for adolescent moves round to the other end

explanation.surface: A cheeky teenage boy whose yearnings keep switching from one camp to another.
explanation.walkthrough: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency yen; it hops from the start of the word to its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouthy is informal for cheeky and given to backchat, a close synonym of impertinent.

clue.text: Ailments put mother on toilet

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: ma is an everyday word for mother
the ladies is a women's public toilet

explanation.surface: Someone's illnesses are blamed on Mum's trip to the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the ladies' is the usual name for a women's lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladies are illnesses or disorders, a straight synonym for ailments.

clue.text: Happy to participate you said with profit generated

indicators.note: the pronoun spoken aloud sounds like a single letter of the alphabet

parts.note: the pronoun, whose spoken form matches a letter

indicators.note: the letters of profit are produced in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells you that you are keen to join in because money has been made.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up for it is an informal idiom for being willing and eager to take part.

clue.text: Shot stern English dons

indicators.note: the word for stern puts on the abbreviation for English like a garment, wearing it inside

parts.note: hard as in severe or strict

explanation.surface: A severe Englishman puts on his academic gown before a shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as a gun firing, but it means moved off fast, a past tense of rushing.
explanation.definitionFit: To hare is to run very fast, so hared is a past-tense synonym of shot, as in shot off.

clue.text: Concerns some French revolutionary lovingly embraced

indicators.note: the French word is turned around, read backwards

parts.note: des is the French word for some

explanation.surface: Worried about some French insurgents, a couple hugged tenderly.
explanation.definitionFit: To caress is to stroke or hold someone with affection, so the past tense fits tender embracing.

clue.text: Gentle sort joining a body of soldiers — he's producing memoir

parts.note: an angel is a kind, gentle person
the SAS is the British Special Air Service regiment

explanation.surface: A mild-mannered man joins an army unit and comes out with his life story.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS is the Special Air Service, a British special forces regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela's Ashes is Frank McCourt's celebrated account of his impoverished Limerick childhood, an example of autobiography.

clue.text: Part of potato starter that's revelatory

definitions.note: a phrase describing a thing, matching the noun answer

parts.note: the eye is the bud on a potato's skin
an opener begins things, like a first course or first match

explanation.surface: Some piece of a potato served as a first course turns out surprisingly illuminating.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is something surprising that shows a person a truth they had not realised.

clue.text: Lot of alcohol sunk if turning fifty

indicators.note: these letters turn into a new arrangement

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone downs drink after drink as they hit their fiftieth birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: A skinful is British slang for enough drink to make someone drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Having had a skinful means having drunk a large quantity, an informal idiom for heavy drinking.

clue.text: Break down joke that's heard to gradually understand

indicators.note: that's heard says the pair of words is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: a machine that dies has broken down; a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: Collapsing at a joke when you hear it, before slowly getting the point.
explanation.walkthrough: DIE JEST, said aloud, sounds like DIGEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To digest information is to absorb and take it in slowly, the way food is processed over time.

clue.text: Long-term cons tons of body-builders avoided

indicators.note: the abbreviation for tons is avoided, left out of the word for body-builders

explanation.surface: Prisoners serving long stretches steer clear of the hefty gym crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence, and cons is slang for convicts.

clue.text: Deciding jointly about getting on ferries

indicators.note: the word for growing old carries the other piece inside it

explanation.surface: Passengers come to a joint decision about boarding the boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on ferries' reads as boarding boats; 'ferries' is a verb meaning carries.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeing means reaching the same decision together, a direct sense of the verb in its participle form.

clue.text: Tips when penning said article succeeded

indicators.note: the word for when encloses the next pieces like a pen holding animals

parts.note: once as in at the time that

explanation.surface: Gratuities are noted while someone writes up a successful oral piece.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the genealogy abbreviation for succeeded.
explanation.definitionFit: Overbalances means loses balance and falls over, a synonym of tips as in topples.

clue.text: Daughter was some time back risk-taker

indicators.note: the two words are read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A daughter existed long ago, who took chances.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is someone recklessly bold, a person who takes dangerous chances.

clue.text: Seabirds getting lost in swells

indicators.note: the word in is lost from the birds

explanation.surface: Seabirds go missing among the waves of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swells' looks like waves, but it is the verb, as in puffs out.
explanation.definitionFit: To puff up is to inflate or swell, so puffs is a verb synonym of swells.

clue.text: Boldly join insurrection taking place in work

parts.note: enter as in sign up to

indicators.note: the word for revolt is placed inside the word for work

parts.note: to ply is to work at a trade

explanation.surface: Bravely joining a rebellion that breaks out at the factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprisingly means in a resourceful, adventurous way, a near synonym of acting with daring.

clue.text: Recording in building having erased top social event

indicators.note: the record goes inside the shortened word
the first letter of the word for building is rubbed out

parts.note: an erection is a built structure
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record made in an edifice whose roof was removed becomes the evening's party.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception is a formal gathering, such as one held after a wedding, to welcome guests.

clue.text: Easiest shot blocked by one in my view

indicators.note: the rearranged letters have the I stuck in among them
ruined, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The simplest attempt at goal is stopped by a single defender, in my opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: As I see it is an idiom introducing a personal opinion, the same as in my view.

clue.text: Horror, as robbers nobbled car parts

indicators.note: tampered with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dismay as thieves tamper with vehicle components.
explanation.walkthrough: To nobble is British slang for tampering with something, originally a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Shock absorbers are the dampers on a vehicle's suspension, so they are examples of components of a car.

clue.text: One stores aged wine in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for wine goes backwards

explanation.surface: A pensioner lays down old vintage after leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder is a person who accumulates and keeps things, so one who stores up supplies.

clue.text: Catch characters in veterans' network after keeling over

indicators.note: those letters are read upside down, from the bottom of the down entry
the answer is made of letters inside these words

explanation.surface: An old soldiers' web trips someone up once they have toppled over.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to trap something, as in a net, a synonym of catch.

clue.text: Fills opening in stapler with staples

indicators.note: the start of the word stapler

parts.note: its first letter is the opening of the word

explanation.surface: Someone loads the slot of a stapler with a fresh supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fills' reads as loading the stapler, but it is the verb for packing shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: To stack shelves is to load them, so stacks works as a synonym of fills.

clue.text: Walk from corner holding mastiff's lead

indicators.note: the word for corner holds the next letter inside it
the leading letter of the word mastiff's

parts.note: the dog's name supplies its leading letter

explanation.surface: Taking a stroll from a street corner while gripping the big dog's leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' pretends to be a dog's leash, but it signals the word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a long, heavy-footed walk, a noun synonym of walk.

clue.text: A sign about hotel services for boozers

indicators.note: the zodiac sign goes about, around, the abbreviation for hotel

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A notice concerning the amenities a hotel offers to heavy drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a boozer is a pub, not just a drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Alehouses are old-fashioned pubs, the taverns that British slang calls boozers.

clue.text: Group of performers regularly boycotted tango

indicators.note: every other letter, taken at regular intervals

parts.note: the word the letters are taken from
T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Musicians kept refusing to play the tango.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is an ensemble of eight musicians or singers.

clue.text: Swimmer with lack of hostility discussed pouchlike garment

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word for absence of conflict matches a word for a bit

explanation.surface: A fish and a truce are talked over alongside a curious item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A codpiece is the pouch worn at the front of men's breeches in Tudor fashion.

clue.text: A kid free from anxiety

explanation.surface: A young goat or child carefree and relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child or goat, but it is the verb meaning to rib.
explanation.definitionFit: At ease means relaxed and comfortable, the opposite of being worried.

clue.text: Suffering Frenchman's put in plea for help

indicators.note: the man's name is placed inside the distress call

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A Frenchman in pain sends out a call for assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Soreness is physical pain or tenderness, so it is a noun synonym of suffering.

clue.text: Shortest route east completely empty road

indicators.note: every word is emptied, keeping only its first and last letters

parts.note: the first word to be emptied
the second word to be emptied
the third word to be emptied

explanation.surface: The quickest way heading east follows a deserted highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a public road in a town, lined with buildings.
